name: MISO
desc: Positions engaging the Midcontinent ISO (MISO) specifically.

letters.desc: AEP groups MISO alongside other regions where ongoing state and RTO-level efforts are underway, arguing federal reforms should be additive rather than preemptive.
quotes: The Commission's reforms should avoid introducing additional delays to large load interconnection by disrupting state and regional-level efforts.

letters.desc: Antora points to MISO as a region whose rules better accommodate flexible loads, allowing large loads that do not increase the coincident peak to interconnect without new capacity requirements, which is why its first commercial project is in MISO rather than SPP.
quotes: MISO allows large loads that do not increase the coincident peak to interconnect without new capacity requirements.

letters.desc: Chevron points to the MISO ERAS order as a precedent for accelerated interconnection study processes that can address near-term resource adequacy needs, supporting FERC endorsement of comparable mechanisms.
quotes: The Commission should be open to such regional fast-track proposals, which may provide mechanisms to connect large loads and generation before DOE ANOPR standards can be practicably established in all regions.

letters.desc: Entergy operates in MISO South under a vertically integrated, retail cost-of-service model and reports that existing MISO and state processes are working to connect large loads. Federal rules must not override these regional frameworks.
quotes: The Entergy Operating Companies believe our existing processes for the interconnection and service to large loads are working, as they balance new customer timelines with secure, reliable, and affordable service to all customers using existing regulatory frameworks.

it is important that the Commission avoid blanket rules that fail to account for such differences.  In particular, Entergy Services urges the Commission to avoid ordering any blanket rules that could interfere with retail jurisdictional resource planning that currently takes place in MISO South, as these processes are working well.

letters.desc: esVolta cites MISO's local resource zone framework as a parallel model, recommending a 90-day expedited study timeline for storage resources in the same LRZ as the large load.
quotes: esVolta would go even further to support approaches in PJM that rightfully identify supply resources in the same "load deliverability area or LDA" as an eligible resource for the expedited interconnection process and similarly, in MISO, standalone storage and other resources that have agreements with large loads to provide needed resources and are located in the same "local resource zone or LRZ" should be deemed eligible for an expedited interconnection process completed within 90 days.

letters.desc: MISO's Expedited Resource Addition Study process demonstrates an effective approach for accelerated interconnections that should be applied to large load customers.
quotes: When reviewing the Secretary's proposal, the Commission should take lessons learned from MISO and SPP to expedite generator interconnections, allow cluster studies and study transmission projects across Regional Transmission Organizations (RTOs).

MISO's recently approved Expedited Resource Addition Study (ERAS) process provides a targeted solution to get needed generation resources interconnected and online to meet the same load challenges as justification for the proposed ANOPR.

letters.desc: ITC highlights MISO's Long-Range Transmission Planning as instrumental in enabling large load growth in Iowa. The filer points to successful coordination between ITC Midwest and MISO to develop LRTP projects efficiently, demonstrating how regional transmission planning can reduce interconnection timelines and upgrade costs.
quotes: ITC Midwest's forward-looking, proactive approach to grid development, reinforced through MISO's Long-Range Transmission Planning ("LRTP") portfolios, has enabled faster large-load interconnections by providing available regional capacity and reducing the scope and cost of network upgrades, benefiting both new customers and existing ratepayers.

A key factor in accommodating the data center growth in Iowa was ITC Midwest's ability to start developing the LRTP projects right after MISO Board approval due to the segments not being eligible for Order No. 1000 competition. If the projects had been subject to the solicitation process, it would have added almost two years of delay before determining who was responsible for construction, irreparably undermining the in-service timeline requirements.

we believe the enormous new loads already in the pipeline are just the beginning. As LRTP projects come online, we are optimistic Iowa will be positioned to accommodate additional data center investment and other future load growth, improving reliability and increasing rate benefits for customers over time.

letters.desc: Missouri PSC highlights MISO's Expedited Project Review process as an effective stakeholder-developed approach that FERC should draw on for its final rule.
quotes: FERC's final rule should draw from existing RTO approaches. Both MISO and SPP developed their large load interconnection provisions through stakeholder engagement, and thus they provide examples of effective approaches that FERC should incorporate into its final rule.

letters.desc: NDPSC supports MISO's Expedited Project Review process for fast-tracking transmission projects needed for large load reliability, demonstrating RTO capability to address the issue.
quotes: MISO established a mechanism, known as the Expedited Project Review process, to quickly study and approve transmission projects that are necessary to meet urgent reliability requirements, many of which are associated with large load additions.

The SPP and MISO approaches to large load interconnection represent well-vetted processes which resulted from significant stakeholder input and buy-in. Both approaches help to address the challenges associated with large load customers while respecting and maintaining state and federal jurisdiction. The NDPSC supports the work the RTOs are doing and would advocate for a similar large load interconnection process, one that is limited in scope and based on demonstrated methodology already in place within RTO's, to be adopted should FERC move forward with a rule making.

letters.desc: MISO's well-vetted Expedited Project Review process balances speed with respect for state and federal jurisdiction while addressing large load integration challenges.
quotes: Like SPP, MISO has worked to facilitate the interconnection of large loads on its system. MISO established a mechanism, known as the Expedited Project Review process, to quickly study and approve transmission projects that are necessary to meet urgent reliability requirements, many of which are associated with large load additions.

The SPP and MISO approaches to large load interconnection represent well-vetted processes which resulted from significant stakeholder input and buy-in. Both approaches help to address the challenges associated with large load customers while respecting and maintaining state and federal jurisdiction.

letters.org: Wisconsin Electric Power CompanyWisconsin Public Service Corporation
letters.desc: WEC points to MISO's load interconnection whitepaper, Expedited Project Review, and new ERAS process as evidence that MISO already addresses large load interconnections effectively. They argue a federal rule applied uniformly across MISO would disrupt rather than improve these efforts.
quotes: the Commission should honor established processes that are working well and should not apply federal rules to regions where there are existing or proposed processes or tariffs, such as in Wisconsin.  At a minimum, the Commission should apply the "independent entity variation" standard to load interconnection rules, as it does the generator interconnection rules.

any rulemaking should ensure that franchised service territories are protected and that any processes mandated by a rule does not permit generators to serve co-located load in violation of retail franchise laws.

letters.desc: The filer highlights that MISO and its transmission owners have already interconnected more than 14.4 GW of large load through processes such as the Expedited Project Review, and warns that federal action would disrupt these effective regional efforts.
quotes: To insert a parallel federal process now risks duplicating these efforts, at best, and injecting delay and triggering litigation, at worst.

the Commission could spur faster, more creative solutions by allowing MISO's industry participants 'to continue focusing attention on efficiently interconnecting large loads pursuant to processes that reflect the unique circumstances of their members, states, stakeholders, and transmission systems'
the Commission should allow MISO and the MISO Transmission Owners to request deviations from any final rule to preserve the funding approach that has worked for the MISO region

letters.desc: Arkansas supported and FERC approved MISO's expedited study process. Combined with ongoing RTO coordination, MISO's region does not need the ANOPR's proposed reforms.
quotes: the proposed rule is unnecessarily harmful for Arkansas and risks disrupting well‑functioning regional and state processes.
there are already processes for the integration of large loads and therefore the proposed ANOPR is unnecessary.

Arkansas supported and FERC recently approved MISO's Expedited Resource Addition Study Process to address faster processes through MISO's interconnection queue, which addresses the issues FERC seeks to remedy.
These reforms are specifically tailored to regional system needs and reflect ongoing coordination among the RTOs, load‑serving entities, transmission owners and state regulators.

letters.desc: As a MISO member, Consumers Energy notes that MISO has already implemented reforms such as the ERAS process to speed generation interconnection. Adding expedited large load study tracks would burden MISO's limited study resources and could undercut those improvements.
quotes: Certain ANOPR proposals, such as the notion that 'the interconnection study of large loads that agree to be curtailable and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable and dispatchable should be expedited,' will burden RTO/ISO resources that are also working to perform timely studies of new generation.

letters.desc: Fluence opposes MISO's practice of assessing transmission service charges on storage withdrawals, which it says conflicts with Order 841, creates a unique competitive disadvantage versus other regions, and deters storage development where it is most needed.
quotes: MISO's practice of charging transmission service for energy storage withdrawals represents a significant barrier to storage development and is potentially in conflict with Order 841's (specifically 841a) directive regarding comparable treatment of energy storage.

No other RTO/ISO applies transmission charges to storage charging in the manner MISO does, creating a significant competitive disadvantage for MISO and a barrier to IPP-based storage development in the region.

letters.org: Louisiana Public Service CommissionMississippi Public Service Commission
letters.desc: Louisiana and Mississippi participate in MISO South through vertically integrated utilities and cooperatives. The commissions say no interconnection delays exist in this region and cite the approval of the $27 billion Meta data center project in under nine months as proof.
quotes: Louisiana and Mississippi have not had any issues associated with the delay of the interconnection of large loads, and FERC should be mindful that any rules adopted could unintentionally result in delays, instead of acceleration of the desired interconnections

This expansion of federal jurisdiction is not needed in MISO South and SPP regions, the members of which mainly consist of vertically integrated utilities and cooperatives, and it is not needed in Louisiana and Mississippi.

any rules adopted should not be a one-size-fits-all proposition. Rules must take into account regional differences. State and RTO processes that have worked well should be accommodated and not changed. Flexibility is crucial to meeting the needs of new large loads and of the affected states.

letters.desc: ATC operates exclusively in the MISO footprint and notes that MISO's tariff already treats all network load as firm. ATC argues that MISO's existing stakeholder-driven planning process already coordinates joint siting of load and generation, limiting the need for new federal mandates in this region.
quotes: in ATC's experience, these large load customers require 24/7, uninterrupted, guaranteed, reliable service.  From ATC's perspective, these customers will have network service, and pursuant to MISO's Tariff, all network load is generally treated as firm service.  Introducing curtailment of network load complicates system management and could create scenarios where other customers' firm load is shed before the 'curtailable' large load.

letters.desc: MISO is cited as a region with surplus wind generation that could absorb AI workloads shifted from a constrained PJM interconnection, illustrating the value of cross-region spatial flexibility.
quotes: If the PJM interconnection is thermally constrained but the MISO region has excess wind generation, an orchestrator can route new inference requests to the MISO facility, for example. This capability acts as a "virtual transmission line." Instead of moving megawatts of electrons across a congested wire to meet a static demand, the system moves the demand for those electrons to a location where power is abundant.

letters.desc: Entergy highlights that MISO's existing large load interconnection processes are functioning well and that its own service territories have successfully interconnected major data centers for Google, Meta, and AWS under efficient state regulatory frameworks.
quotes: the Commission cannot automatically extrapolate specific claims made about load interconnections in one area to other parts of the country

there is no evidence that would support a finding that load interconnections in MISO generally, or the service territories of the Entergy Operating Companies specifically, are unjust, unreasonable, or unduly discriminatory or preferential

letters.desc: The filing documents a MISO summer capacity price increase of 2,122% in a single auction year, reflecting the same large-load-driven supply squeeze affecting Illinois ratepayers in the Ameren Illinois service area.
quotes: In the MISO area the summer capacity price increased by an astonishing $635 per MW-day, or approximately 2,122%, from $30 MW-day to $666.50 MW-day.

large load projects create significant risks, including the risks of: (1) insufficient supply to meet existing demand and the additional demand of large load projects, (2) skyrocketing prices both in response to insufficient supply and to provide "incentives" in the hope that increased generator revenues will cause them to build sufficient generation to meet the large load demand, and (3) electricity shortages leading to blackouts or "load shed."

letters.desc: The filer identifies MISO-territory Rust Belt industrial districts as carrying grid characteristics well suited to the stiff-point framework, with high fault-level substations engineered for heavy manufacturing loads that persist even after those industries have departed. MISO is named as a jurisdiction that should file tariff amendments for demand caps.
quotes: Legacy Rust Belt industrial districts carry precisely the grid characteristics that the stiff-point framework rewards. The industrial districts that supported heavy manufacturing, integrated steel production, and automotive assembly during the postwar decades required, and received, high-capacity transmission lines and substations engineered to absorb the kind of volatile, nonlinear loads that are exceptionally difficult to manage on a regional network.

PJM, MISO, SPP, and other RTOs and ISOs operating under FERC jurisdiction should file tariff amendments implementing node-level demand caps for large-load interconnection. Caps should be set at the fault-level capacity available at each interconnection point, net of existing committed load.

RTOs and ISOs should establish a priority processing track for large-load interconnection applications at nodes with demonstrated stiff-point characteristics. Legacy heavy industrial sites in the Rust Belt corridor that carried industrial loads of comparable or greater magnitude within the past thirty years should be eligible for expedited preliminary qualification based on documented interconnection history.

letters.desc: MISO documents its existing processes, including the EPR, ERAS, and LRTP, and notes approximately 17 GW of large load approvals since 2022 and a growing EPR pipeline, to show that regional processes are already delivering results.
quotes: under MISO's existing processes, since the 2022 MTEP cycle, MISO has approved approximately 17 GW of large load additions.

if the Commission decides to move forward with standard large load interconnection procedures, it should also consider how to mitigate the potential increase in congestion along the seam(s) that could result from the interconnection of large loads.

letters.desc: The MISO Transmission Owners document the region's progress: 14.4 GW of large load additions approved since 2022, a draft MTEP25 covering 11.6 GW more, and the new ERAS fast-track process. They use this track record to argue that federal intervention is unnecessary in the MISO footprint.
quotes: since the 2022 MTEP cycle, the MISO Transmission Owners have sought to build, and MISO has approved, the needed transmission enhancements to accommodate approximately 14.4 gigawatts ("GW") of large load additions.

In order to comment meaningfully on the Third Principle, more information is needed.  In the MISO region, load integration and generation interconnection are studied separately because they have separate impacts on the bulk electric system.

large load owners should only be able to co-locate and contract for power directly from generators to the extent state laws and regulations allow.  Second, it is critical to both system planning and operational awareness that load and generation are studied and metered separately, on a gross rather than a net basis.

Under long-standing Commission precedent, the costs of network upgrades required to interconnect load are allocated to transmission customers through transmission rates under Schedule 9 of the MISO Tariff.  LSEs, in turn, pass on those costs to their retail customers.

letters.desc: OMS notes that MISO has no interconnection backlog for large loads and that existing processes, including the Expedited Project Review, already coordinate transmission, resource adequacy, and state oversight effectively. Any federal rule should account for this regional context.
quotes: load interconnection study processes have been working well within the MISO footprint and there are no bottlenecks for interconnecting and energizing large loads that need attention in MISO.
many other states have approved or are considering large load tariffs that all contemplate a range of 100-150 MW.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The group notes that MISO shares SPP's characteristics of vertically-integrated utilities and lower transmission density, distinguishing both from PJM's retail-open-access structure.
quotes: the characteristics of regions such as SPP and MISO that are largely composed of vertically-integrated and investor-owned utilities are materially different than other regions, such as PJM, that include numerous states with retail open access policies as well as several wires-only transmission and distribution utilities.

letters.desc: The filer cites MISO data showing that ambient and emergency ratings could have saved $168 million in real-time congestion costs in Winter 2023, and notes MISO has taken incremental steps including a congestion reconfiguration process.
quotes: we urge the Commission to encourage all RTOs to host forums to investigate the opportunity for ATTs and other solutions to increase capacity and improve affordability and how to integrate ATTs into all aspects of an RTO's processes.

letters.desc: WIRES cites MISO's approval of a $21 billion long range transmission plan as an example of regional efforts already underway.
quotes: in December 2024, MISO approved the $21 billion Tranche 2.1 Long Range Transmission Plan Portfolio.
